tool_input.title: shop namespace: label collision causes partial 5xx via Service endpoint pool
tool_input.content:
**Incident:** HighErrorRate [warning] namespace=shop service=frontend, ~31% 5xx on /api/, cluster aurora-lab (kind-aurora-lab, kubeconfig-39a45b491ad13aa3).

**Root cause:** Service `api` in namespace `shop` selects pods purely on label `app: api`. A second, unrelated/incomplete Deployment `shop-api` was created with pod template labels `{app: api, app.kubernetes.io/name: shop-api}` — the extra `app: api` label caused its single pod to be silently added to the `api` Service's endpoints alongside the 2 legitimate `api` Deployment pods. `shop-api`'s code (configmap `shop-api`, "shop-api 0.9.3") references `os.environ["DATABASE_URL"]`, which was never set (no Secret/env for it exists in the namespace) — causing a KeyError -> HTTP 500 on every request to that pod. Since the Service round-robins across 3 endpoints (2 healthy + 1 always-broken), ~33% of frontend `/api/` calls failed, matching the alert's 31%.

**Why this matters:** Kubernetes Services match on labels only — they do not care about Deployment ownership. Any new Deployment whose pod template accidentally reuses an existing Service's selector label (e.g. copy-pasted `app: api`) will be silently load-balanced into that Service's traffic, even if it's a completely different/unfinished app. This is especially dangerous in this cluster because deployments appear to be spun up quickly for testing (shop-api was created only 9s after the core api/frontend/redis stack).

**How to apply / detect quickly:**
1. On a HighErrorRate alert, don't assume the Deployment matching the Service name is the only backend — run `kubectl get endpoints <svc> -o wide` and cross-check IP count against `kubectl get pods -l <svc's selector> ` and `kubectl get deploy -o wide` replica counts. A mismatch (more endpoints than the "obvious" deployment's replicas) means another deployment's pods are leaking into the Service via label overlap.
2. `kubectl get pods -n <ns> --show-labels` to spot pods with the colliding label but a different `app.kubernetes.io/name` or different owning ReplicaSet.
3. Fix: scale the rogue/incomplete deployment to 0 immediately (fast mitigation), then permanently fix by giving it a distinct label (requires delete+recreate since Deployment selector is immutable).
4. Resource/node metrics were normal in this incident (negligible CPU/mem, all nodes Ready) — this class of issue is purely a selector/label config problem, not capacity.
